prompt: An endpoint served 100 requests: 99 took 10 ms and one hit a 5,000 ms timeout. What are the mean and median latency?

options.explanation: These are swapped. The outlier pulls the mean up; the median, the middle value, stays at 10 ms.
Correct. Total latency is 5,990 milliseconds across 100 requests, so the mean is 59.9 milliseconds. Both middle sorted values are 10 milliseconds, giving that median.
Replacing one 10 ms request with a 5,000 ms request raises the mean by (5000 − 10)/100 = 49.9 ms.
2,505 is the average of the two distinct values (10 and 5,000), ignoring that 99 requests were 10 ms.

workedExample:
```formula
x̄ = (99 × 10 ms + 5000 ms) / 100
x̄ = (990 ms + 5000 ms) / 100
x̄ = 59.9 ms
M = (x_(50) + x_(51)) / 2 = 10 ms
where
x̄: "x-bar", the mean latency, in milliseconds (ms)
M: the median, for 100 values the average of the 50th and 51st smallest
x_(50), x_(51): the 50th and 51st smallest latencies, both 10 ms
ms: milliseconds, thousandths of a second
In words: one timeout lifts the mean six-fold to 59.9 ms, while the median stays at 10 ms.
```

A single outlier moves the mean six-fold and the median not at all. Mean resource service time helps estimate total resource work; elapsed latency also includes waiting. For the typical experience in this latency sample, report the median.
